transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

A horrible noise can come from a few different places depending on when you hear it. It could be something simple caught in the drain pump (like a coin), worn drum bearings, or failed suspension springs causing banging. To help narrow this down, when exactly does the noise happen (e.g. during filling, washing/tumbling, draining, or spinning) and what does it sound like (e.g. grinding, clunking, screeching, or loud banging)?
It's mainly when it spins, a loud roaring rumble like a jet engine. Gets louder as the spin speeds up. A bit noisy when washing too but much quieter.

A loud roaring rumble that gets louder as the spin speed increases is very characteristic of worn drum bearings. This happens when the internal bearing assembly wears out, allowing the drum to wobble and create significant friction and noise. To confirm this, please switch off and unplug the machine first. Then open the door and try to push the top of the drum down firmly with your hand. Does it feel loose with a clunking play at the bottom (indicating worn bearings), or does it move only slightly with firm springy resistance?
Yes there's a noticeable clunky up and down play when I lift the edge of the drum. Is it worth fixing?

With that clunky play in the drum combined with the jet-engine roar on spin, it is almost certainly worn drum bearings. Whether it is worth fixing depends largely on the age of the machine and its replacement cost. If your washing machine is less than five years old, a professional repair might be worthwhile as it restores the appliance to like-new condition. However, if it is older or you are considering an upgrade anyway, the labour and parts for this job can sometimes approach the price of a new machine. To help you weigh up the options properly, I need to know exactly what model you have. Could you please tell me the brand and model number? You'll usually find this on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back panel.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi ZWF81443W, read off the door label. It's about 9 years old and cost around £350 new.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
With that clunky play in the drum combined with the jet-engine roar on spin, it is almost certainly worn drum bearings (and often the spider they are mounted on). This is a major repair because it requires completely dismantling the machine to access the rear of the tub. Given your Zanussi ZWF81443W is 9 years old and originally cost around £350, the labour and parts for this job will likely approach or exceed the price of a new machine. It is generally not worth fixing at this stage; I would recommend looking into replacing the appliance instead.
